root_idea.summary: An underlying state of stillness joined with covering or enclosure.
root_idea.development: From stillness and covering: night settles into quiet and may spread darkness over what it contains; related derivatives extend to calm or unruffled states and to covering a body.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Classical Arabic Form I perfect citation form سَجَا rather than the inflected Quranic spelling سَجَىٰ.

senses.definition: To become still, quiet, or calm.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَا, said of the night; the reading may also convey that its people have become silent or that its darkness is at rest.

senses.definition: Of the night, to become dark, for its darkness to spread, or to cover and conceal with darkness.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternate Quran-attested interpretation of وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَا, describing the extension or enveloping effect of the night’s darkness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become still, quiet, or calm, especially said of the sea or wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Classical applications include a sea whose waves have become calm and a wind that has become still.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to prolong her cry of yearning toward her young.
To cover something; especially, to cover or shroud a dead person with a garment or piece of cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the Form II covering construction, including the conventional use for covering the dead.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To touch something, including, in the recorded food expression, to partake of it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes an object; the food example uses the verb for touching or eating from what was brought.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To work or labor upon something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of working at or cultivating a landed estate; the precise role of others in that cultivation is left uncertain in the evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, to have much milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded in the Form IV entry in connection with the expression اسجت الناقةُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A natural or innate disposition, temperament, or firmly rooted quality of character.
Still, quiet, or unruffled: said of a she-camel while being milked, smooth fur or wool, or a gentle wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are recorded applications of the feminine adjective to a camel, animal covering, and wind respectively.
In the recorded expression, it describes a woman’s eye or glance as an accessory to beauty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Still, calm, or motionless; applied to the sea, a calm night, or an eye.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A calm night is described as having still wind and clouds and little darkness; an eye may likewise be motionless or have a languid look.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the Quranic stillness and darkness readings and the broader calm applications.
Form II covering and shrouding construction.
Unruffled fur and wool are covered by the same adjective branch.
Gentle wind is covered by the same stillness branch.
Still or calm adjective applications, including the eye sense.

cautions: The single Quran occurrence supports both a stillness reading and a darkness or covering reading; these are distinct attested interpretations of the same construction, not separate occurrences.

The Form IV Lane entry places the milk-related statement under أَسْجَوَ while its subentry text prints اسجت الناقةُ; the lexical statement is clear, but the exact displayed inflection is not normalized beyond the entry heading.
